cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus invites a little child to stand among them. The disciples ask a big question, and Jesus doesn't give them a speech first. He invites a little child to stand among them (Matthew 18:2). Sometimes the best answer is just a little one standing right there, friends.

The answer is that you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven." (Matthew 18:3). He starts with "Truly I tell you…" so everyone knows He means it. The change He talks about is becoming like little children.

The answer is whoever humbles himself like this little child. Jesus says, "Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven." (Matthew 18:4). The disciples asked who ranks highest, and Jesus invited a little child to stand among them. I'm still waiting on a trophy for MY humility, friends, which tells you how I'm doing.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me." (Matthew 18:5). Think about that one, bakers. A simple welcome in His name, and Jesus says it's welcoming Him.

The answer is the man through whom they come. Jesus says, "These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!" (Matthew 18:7). It's a serious line, friends, and I think it shows how much Jesus cares about those little ones.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire." (Matthew 18:8). Entering life is the better thing, even if it costs you. It's a heavy teaching, friends, and Jesus says it plainly.

The answer is that their angels in heaven always see His Father's face. Jesus says, "For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven." (Matthew 18:10). That's the reason He gives for not looking down on any of these little ones. I think it's worth a slow read, bakers.

The answer is that the man leaves the ninety-nine and searches for the lost one. Jesus asks, "…will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?" (Matthew 18:12). One sheep out of a hundred has gone astray, and the man goes out to search for it.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "…he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray." (Matthew 18:13). Look at that word, friends, "more." That's the whole answer.

The answer is that He is not willing that any little one should perish. Jesus says, "In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish." (Matthew 18:14). The shepherd's search is the picture, bakers, and the Father's heart is the point.

The answer is that you have won your brother over. Jesus says, "If he listens to you, you have won your brother over." (Matthew 18:15). Notice what you win, friends: your brother. Getting him back is the prize.

The answer is to take one or two others along. Jesus says, "But if he will not listen, take one or two others along…" (Matthew 18:16). The talk stays small, bakers. One or two others join you, and that's the next step.

The answer is witnesses. The words are "every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses." (Matthew 18:16). Jesus is quoting Deuteronomy 19:15. So the one or two others you bring can speak up about what happened, friends.

The answer is the church. Jesus says, "If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church." (Matthew 18:17). It goes from private, to one or two others, to the church. Each step gets a little wider, bakers.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector." (Matthew 18:17). That's the last step in the list, friends. It comes only after the private talk, the one or two others and the church.

The answer is His Father in heaven. Jesus says, "…if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven." (Matthew 18:19). When two of you on the earth agree about what you ask for, bakers, it is the Father who does it.

The answer is Jesus Himself. Jesus says, "For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them." (Matthew 18:20). "…there am I…" means Jesus is speaking about Himself. Two or three people gathered in His name, friends, and He's with them.
